questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me, it was very important to choose a country that was far away from Denmark, to try something completely new. I also wanted to go somewhere where the main language is Spanish.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was the best experience of my life.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find information. However, everything was going a bit slow. When you contact UDLAP, it takes some days for them to answer - if not some weeks...

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When you arrive at Cholula, you will immediately get in contact with old students from UDLAP, who will help you through the whole process. They make a Whatsapp group for all the international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. There are a lot of international houses - cheap and cozy. I lived in the house called Casa Roja, and I think it's the best house! I will for sure recommend this one or Casa Real.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's amazing. You will easily get friends and the security for all the international houses is on top.  Cameras on the street for example.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think it was very easy. They have a catalog where you can see which classes you can take in the semester you are going. However, the catalog is only coming some weeks before the semester starts, which can be a little bit stressful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can write to the teachers if you have any doubts.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much. The system is not so strict.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had five courses - i don't remember the level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's very different since the class is only for one hour and then you switch to another class. You only have two hours each week for each class. And there are a lot of presentations and exams. However, they are all very easy.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Organizational Psychology 
Leadership and negotiation 
Leadership and teamwork
Food and life
Human rights

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I LOVED human rights! Best class at UDLAP, and the professor, Samuel Stone, is amazing! Best professor I have had in my life. 
Also Gabriela Diaz is an excellent teacher, she is very kind and always ready to help you!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The first three months of my stay the university was closed. So I didn't experience the campus very well.  The last two months yes, but then I didn't have the time since I had a lot of exams and travels. However, the campus is very pretty! I loved to spend time there.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't really know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Again, hard to say when the campus was closed.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I loved Chiapas, Oaxaca, Atlixco, Guanajuato, Sayulita!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy enough! You should however get used to the Latin-American time. If someone tells you, that they will be there in 5 minutes, never believe them. It will be a least 30 minutes. Never be there in time. You will wait and look like a fool. Another thing, you will get friends after 10 minutes everywhere you go. People are so friendly, they always want to talk and get to know you. Don't be shy! Just enjoy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people! I love Mexicans. They are so friendly and warm. You are never alone in Mexico. When I arrived to Mexico, it was two days before New Year's Eve, and I had nowhere to go. A girl i only had been in contact with on Whatsapp (one of the old students of UDLAP) invited me to her house with her family to spend the evening with them! This will rarely happen in Denmark, but here it will occur at least 10 times during your stay. Mexican people are great.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Read all the reviews on this website - it really helps you to get an idea of everything! 
Everything is gonna be cool! Cholula, the city of UDLAP, is amazing! Best city in Mexico.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy every moment, time flies!
And bring warm clothes, it gets very cold at night.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get to know another culture. You get a new perspective on life. Be ready to visit a place that is completely different from your own daily life. Churches every 20 meters, noises every night from dogs, churches, or fireworks. A lot of fireworks, and no, not the ones that are pretty. Only a big noise... And in the first two weeks, you think someone is getting shot every time. However, it is just churches felicitating something, and that is EVERY day. Get used to it. You are not going to sleep the first weeks, so party instead! In addition, it's also a poor country, with kids on the street selling bubble gums, old people of the age of 100 still working in the markets to support their families, and people working 70 hours each week for no money. However, they still smile and keep having hope. They are grateful for living. They are not complaining about it, at least not the ones I have spoken to. Maybe Denmark is one of the happiest countries, but I don't really know how it is possible. We are always stressed or depressed. Here in Mexico, they just live. Even though life sucks. I want to have the same life perspective as them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To not be scared. To have trust in people. To walk in the street alone, without being nervous. However, you get used to it. And you understand the norms. In the day, yes. In the night. maybe not. Mexico is not dangerous if you take care. Just don't be stupid.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: ENJOY.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
